depth: The monocular depth image shows a sharply downward first-person view across a woven, bamboo-framed cot (~0.5–1.0 m below the camera) and the level floor behind it (~1.3–1.6 m away). The camera wearer’s pink-covered lap and bent right arm form the brightest and closest surfaces at ~0.3–0.6 m. A mint-green knitted section with needles on the left and a yarn ball in the center lie within the wearer’s immediate reach (~0.4–0.8 m), whereas a white cloth, purple material, and the striped left arm and hand of a second person occupy a somewhat lower, more distant area on the cot’s right side (~0.7–1.0 m from the wearer and ~0.2 m beside the wearer’s elbow). Past the cot’s front-right bamboo rail, above the dark floor surface, a third person’s crossed legs and sandal-clad feet appear in darker grey at ~1.2–1.6 m, approximately ~0.5 m beyond the cot edge and second person. The heads of all three people are outside the image, so no gaze directed at the wearer is visible; orientation can only be inferred from limbs pointing roughly forward or diagonally away from the cot. Between frames 1 and 2, the camera turns and pitches a little to the right while the wearer’s right hand pulls back from the knitted material on the left and remains across their chest through frame 5. This brings both people on the right farther into view as the floor broom (~1.3 m away) moves upward and left. Relative to RGB, depth separates the raised cot plane and wearer’s elevated forearm from the sunken floor much more clearly and captures the yarn ball’s 3D shape and the fine knitting needles. It remains unreliable over the floor, however, where the broom vanishes into even darkness, and in frame 1, where the bamboo rail and rope weave of the cot collapse into one smooth slope.
segmentation: The instance-segmentation view tries to divide the downward-facing scene into individual “person” masks over an unlabelled black background. Its main detection is the camera wearer’s torso, pink clothing, and right arm in the lower-central foreground (~0.3–0.7 m from the camera and within immediate self-reach). Beginning in frame 2, distinct masks along the lower-right and upper-right borders identify the partly hidden person seated next to the wearer on the cot (~0.6–0.9 m away, within the wearer’s arm’s reach and the white cloth) and the third person sitting on the floor past the cot’s front-right rail (~1.2–1.6 m away and ~0.5 m from the cot edge), who holds a plastic bag within their own reach in frame 5. After frame 1, the camera pans slightly right as the wearer’s right arm leaves the knitting on the left and lies horizontally across their torso in frames 2–5, causing the right-side person masks to occupy more of the image. Every head nevertheless remains outside the frame, and nobody is visibly looking at the camera wearer. The masks help separate the wearer’s right shoulder from the neighboring person’s lower-right arm, an area where the colorful textiles blend together in RGB, but they exclude every non-person item, including the yarn, knitting needles, fabrics, cot, and broom. Detection is also very unreliable between frames: a hollow area is left inside the wearer’s bent right arm, instance colours change from frame to frame, and the bamboo cot rail, woven ropes, white cloth, and floor broom are incorrectly classified as “person” areas in frames 1, 3, and 5.
pose: The pose visualization draws 2D skeletal landmarks against black, finding no skeleton at all in frame 1 and only one magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer’s right hand in frames 2–5, positioned about 0.4–0.5 m ahead of and beneath the camera. Throughout frames 2 to 5, the magenta hand stays still on the left side of the wearer’s chest, within reach of both the nearby yarn ball (~0.5 m away) and the knitted material on the left, after withdrawing from the frame’s left edge between frames 1 and 2 while the camera moved slightly right. Only in frame 5 does a yellow face-and-body keypoint skeleton emerge on the right, stretching from the cot surface (~0.7 m away) toward the upper-right floor (~1.3 m away). Everything else, including the wearer’s torso, the cot, the yarn, and the broom on the floor, is entirely absent from the rendering. By removing the RGB clutter of pink garments and green wool, this sparse skeleton display clearly isolates the wearer’s resting right hand, including its precise finger articulation and leftward orientation. Nevertheless, it is broadly unreliable for understanding the complete scene: the wearer’s hand is missed in frame 1; the neighboring person’s hand and the floor-seated person’s legs and hands go undetected in frames 1–4; and frame 5 invents one deformed yellow head-and-torso skeleton over the white cloth and adjoining arms even though no head is actually within the field of view.
